accepted.s: The Andhra circle of the Congress was formed in which year after the Calcutta Congress accepted the demand for linguistic organisation?
accepted.x: The Calcutta Congress of 1917 accepted the demand, and the Andhra circle was formed in January 1918.
accepted.tq: Use the event-to-year link and distinguish the acceptance year from the formation year.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: Who was the first president of the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee, whose presidential term is given as 1918–1923?
accepted.x: Konda Venkatappayya is identified as the first president of the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee, with his term given as 1918–1923.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the first committee president and the first president of the separate Andhra Congress Committee.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the formation of the separate Andhra Congress Committee:
1. It was formed on 22 January 1918.
2. Nyapati Subba Rao was its first president.
3. Konda Venkatappayya was its first secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The separate Andhra Congress Committee was formed on 22 January 1918, with Nyapati Subba Rao as president and Konda Venkatappayya as secretary.
accepted.tq: Check the date, office-holder and office separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two leadership descriptions associated with the Andhra Congress organisation in 1918?
o: Konda Venkatappayya was first president of the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee, while Nyapati Subba Rao was first president of the separate Andhra Congress Committee.
Nyapati Subba Rao was first secretary of the Provincial Committee, while Konda Venkatappayya was president of the separate committee.
Pattabhi Sitaramayya was first president of both bodies, while B.N. Sarma was secretary.
Nyapati Subba Rao was first president of both bodies, while Konda Venkatappayya was secretary of both.
accepted.x: Konda Venkatappayya is given as the first president of the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee, whereas Nyapati Subba Rao was the first president of the separate Andhra Congress Committee.
accepted.tq: Separate similar organisational labels before matching each office-holder.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: The demand for a separate Andhra circle was taken to the All-India Congress Committee by which session of the Andhra Mahasabha?
o: The special session at Guntur in 1918
accepted.x: The fourth Andhra Mahasabha in 1916 took the demand to the AICC, which referred it to the provincial bodies in December 1916.
accepted.tq: Link the organisational demand with the specific Mahasabha session and year.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: At Lucknow in 1916, the All-India Congress Committee, while examining the Andhra demand,
o: rejected the demand as harmful to national unity
referred the demand to the Montagu-Chelmsford Committee
examined the demand but took no decision
accepted the demand and immediately formed Andhra Province
accepted.x: The AICC examined the demand at Lucknow in 1916 but took no decision. Pattabhi Sitaramayya pressed the demand there with Tilak’s support.
accepted.tq: Distinguish examination of a proposal from its acceptance or rejection.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: Which of the following was a reason advanced by the Andhras for demanding a separate Congress circle in 1914?
o: The Simon Commission had recommended abolition of provincial committees.
Although 256 Andhra delegates attended the Madras Congress, none was placed on the Working Committee.
The Montagu declaration had excluded all Telugu-speaking areas.
The Andhra delegates were denied admission to the Congress session.
accepted.x: At the 1914 Madras Congress, 256 Andhra delegates attended, but no Andhra member was placed on the Working Committee. Tamils also blocked an Andhra resolution.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive numerical detail to identify the correct cause.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: Who pushed the province question at the Madras Provincial Conference in May 1915?
o: Venkatapati Raju of the Madras Council
accepted.x: N. Ekambara Aiyer of Nandyal pressed the province question at the May 1915 Madras Provincial Conference, which refused to discuss it.
accepted.tq: Match the local leader with the specific conference intervention.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: The Andhra demand was strengthened by citing which precedent?
o: The creation of the North-West Frontier Province
The formation of separate linguistic circles for Bihar and Orissa
The division of Punjab into two provinces
The creation of Bengal and Bombay Presidencies
accepted.x: The Andhras cited Bihar and Orissa’s separate circles as a precedent for their own demand.
accepted.tq: Identify the supporting precedent rather than the later constitutional developments.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Andhra movement between 1921 and 1935 is NOT correct?
o: Moderates such as Radhakrishnan, Sir Vijaya and C.R. Reddy kept the Mahasabha going.
The Congress in office in Madras had already completely taken over the demand in 1921.
The movement merged into Gandhian mass struggles.
The phase was described as ‘Swarajya within Swarajya’.
accepted.x: The Congress in office in Madras took over the demand from the declining Mahasabha only from 1946 onwards. The other statements correctly describe the 1921–1935 phase.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that shifts a stated development to the wrong period.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Andhra circle
B. Fourth Andhra Mahasabha taking the demand to the AICC
C. Andhra Provincial Congress Conference at Kadapa
D. Nagpur Congress reorganisation of provincial committees on linguistic lines
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 1916 fourth Mahasabha, January 1918 Andhra circle, 1918 Kadapa conference, and 1920 Nagpur Congress.
accepted.tq: Place the two 1918 events before the 1920 Nagpur reorganisation, while retaining the 1916 starting point.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: The Nagpur Congress of 1920 is associated with which organisational change?
o: Creation of the Andhra State from Madras
Reorganisation of Congress provincial committees on linguistic lines
Submission of the Andhra memorandum to Montagu in London
accepted.x: The Nagpur Congress in 1920 reorganised Congress provincial committees on linguistic lines.
accepted.tq: Match a major Congress session with its specific organisational decision.
accepted.sec: Andhra Provincial Congress Committee - formation year, first president

accepted.s: Who moved the separate-province resolution in 1917?
accepted.x: B.N. Sarma moved the separate-province resolution in 1917.
accepted.tq: Use the action-person association rather than the later memorandum and deputation links.
accepted.sec: Memorandums and deputations to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms → year

accepted.s: The declaration of 20 August 1917 by Montagu dealt with
o: the boycott of the Simon Commission
the formation of the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee
accepted.x: Montagu’s declaration of 20 August 1917 concerned self-governing institutions.
accepted.tq: Identify the subject of the declaration without confusing it with the later Andhra deputation.
accepted.sec: Memorandums and deputations to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms → year

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Montagu-Chelmsford Report of July 1918?
o: It accepted the All-India Linguistic States Conference proposal.
It made no provision for Andhra.
It provided for a separate Andhra province.
accepted.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report of July 1918 made no provision for Andhra.
accepted.tq: Test the precise omission in the reform report rather than assuming that the deputation succeeded.
accepted.sec: Memorandums and deputations to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms → year

accepted.s: The special Mahasabha held in response to the absence of an Andhra provision in the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms was held at
accepted.x: A special Mahasabha was held at Guntur on 17 August 1918 after the July 1918 reforms made no provision for Andhra.
accepted.tq: Combine venue and date to distinguish the Guntur session from the Vijayawada delegation.
accepted.sec: Memorandums and deputations to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms → year

accepted.s: At the special Mahasabha at Guntur in 1918, Pattabhi Sitaramayya proposed
o: a deputation to the Round Table Conference
the transfer of Bellary to Madras
a boycott of the Simon Commission
accepted.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya proposed an All-India Linguistic States Conference at the special Guntur Mahasabha.
accepted.tq: Match the proposal with the meeting at which it was made.
accepted.sec: Memorandums and deputations to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms → year

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. December 1917 — Delegation led by Nyapati Subba Rao met Montagu in Madras
a. December 1918 — Memorandum submitted in London by Mocherla Ramachandra Rao
c. 1918 — Venkatapati Raju moved a matching resolution in the Madras Council
d. 1931 — V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to London in connection with the second Round Table Conference
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. They describe the successive deputations, memorandum, legislative resolution and the 1931 Round Table Conference-related effort.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure date-person pair and verify each event chronologically.
accepted.sec: Memorandums and deputations to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms → year

accepted.s: The December 1918 delegation from the Vijayawada Andhra Provincial Congress Committee submitted its memorandum at
accepted.x: The delegation sent by the Vijayawada Andhra Provincial Congress Committee submitted a memorandum in London through Mocherla Ramachandra Rao.
accepted.tq: Use the location-person association to distinguish the London deputation from the Madras meeting.
accepted.sec: Memorandums and deputations to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms → year

accepted.s: Who reminded the Madras Council in 1928 about the delay in dealing with the Andhra demand?
accepted.x: A. Kaleswara Rao reminded the Madras Council in 1928 about the delay concerning the Andhra demand.
accepted.tq: Match the reminder in the legislature with its year and speaker.
accepted.sec: Memorandums and deputations to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms → year

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the events of 1931 is correct?
o: The Andhra resolution was given to Gandhi for the first Round Table Conference, and Bobbili Raja alone attended it.
The Andhra resolution was given to Gandhi for the second Round Table Conference, while V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to London and Bobbili Raja and Mocherla Ramachandra Rao attended the Conference.
The Simon Commission accepted the Andhra resolution and sent it to London.
The Montagu delegation submitted a memorandum to Gandhi for the second Round Table Conference in Madras.
accepted.x: In 1931, the Andhra resolution was given to Gandhi for the second Round Table Conference; V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to London, and Bobbili Raja and Mocherla Ramachandra Rao attended the Conference.
accepted.tq: Check the conference number, destination and persons together to reject swapped details.
accepted.sec: Memorandums and deputations to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms → year

accepted.s: Which of the following was a response of Tamil settlers to the Andhra movement?
o: They opposed the movement, with Pillais and Ayyars among the Tamil settlers associated with the opposition.
They proposed the All-India Linguistic States Conference.
They demanded that Telugu become the sole language of Madras Presidency.
They led the delegation to Montagu in December 1917.
accepted.x: Tamil settlers, including Pillais and Ayyars, opposed the Andhra movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the social group associated with opposition rather than the leaders of the Andhra demand.
accepted.sec: Madras politicians' response and Tamil opposition

accepted.s: Which statement best represents the argument published by an Andhra Patrika writer in response to Tamil opposition?
o: Only a common Madras province could preserve national unity.
Linguistic provinces were incompatible with the Congress organisation.
Tamil separation from Telugu areas would destroy national unity.
Tamils separating from Telugus would not harm national unity.
accepted.x: The Andhra Patrika writer argued that Tamils separating from Telugus would not harm national unity.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the stated argument and its deliberately reversed version.
accepted.sec: Madras politicians' response and Tamil opposition

accepted.s: Which of the following groups consisted of Telugu opponents of the Andhra movement mentioned in connection with Madras politics?
o: Guthi Kesava Pillai, Doraiswami Ayyangar and Gopalaswamy Mudaliar
Nyapati Subba Rao, Konda Venkatappayya and Pattabhi Sitaramayya
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, A. Kaleswara Rao and B.N. Sarma
V.V. Jogayya Pantulu, Bobbili Raja and Mocherla Ramachandra Rao
accepted.x: The Telugu opponents named were Guthi Kesava Pillai, Doraiswami Ayyangar of Chittoor and Gopalaswamy Mudaliar of Bellary.
accepted.tq: Separate opponents from the leaders and supporters of the Andhra movement.
accepted.sec: Madras politicians' response and Tamil opposition

accepted.s: Doraiswami Ayyangar, who opposed the Andhra movement, was associated with which place?
accepted.x: Doraiswami Ayyangar of Chittoor was among the Telugu opponents of the Andhra movement.
accepted.tq: Match the individual opponent with the place specifically associated with him.
accepted.sec: Madras politicians' response and Tamil opposition

accepted.s: Gopalaswamy Mudaliar, mentioned among the Telugu opponents of the Andhra movement, was associated with
accepted.x: Gopalaswamy Mudaliar of Bellary was listed among the Telugu opponents of the Andhra movement.
accepted.tq: Use the person-place pair to distinguish the two named regional opponents.
accepted.sec: Madras politicians' response and Tamil opposition
